metadata.title: feat: integrate Langfuse LLM observability via OTEL
metadata.author: crivetimihai

description:
## Summary

- Add Langfuse as an LLM observability backend, receiving traces via standard OTLP/HTTP
- New `docker-compose.with-langfuse.yml` overlay with 6 services (web, worker, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, MinIO, Redis)
- Makefile targets: `make langfuse-up`, `langfuse-down`, `langfuse-status`, `langfuse-logs`, `langfuse-clean`, `langfuse-monitoring-up`
- Full documentation at `docs/docs/manage/observability/langfuse.md`
- `.env.example` section with all Langfuse configuration variables

## Design Decisions

- **Follows Phoenix overlay pattern** (`docker-compose.with-phoenix.yml` precedent)
- **Separate infrastructure** — Langfuse uses its own PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse, MinIO to avoid coupling
- **OTLP/HTTP** — Langfuse does not support gRPC; gateway override sets `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http`
- **Hyphenated service names** — AWS S3 SDK rejects underscore hostnames (`langfuse-minio` not `langfuse_minio`)
- **No host port bindings** for infrastructure — only Langfuse UI exposed on port 3100 (avoids conflicts with Grafana on 3000)
- **Auto-provisioned** org, project, and API keys via `LANGFUSE_INIT_*` env vars — works out of the box

## Test plan

- [x] `docker compose config --quiet` validates with Langfuse overlay
- [x] `docker compose config --quiet --profile monitoring` validates combined stack
- [x] All 6 Langfuse services start healthy (`make langfuse-status`)
- [x] Gateway OTEL exporter initializes and connects to Langfuse
- [x] Tool invocations generate traces visible in Langfuse API (`/api/public/traces`)
- [x] 13+ traces verified flowing from tool calls and health checks into Langfuse v3.162.0
- [x] `make test-mcp-cli` — 17/23 passed (5 failures pre-existing, unrelated to Langfuse)
- [x] No S3 upload errors after hostname fix
- [x] `make langfuse-up/down/status/logs/clean` targets all work

reviews.author: lucarlig
reviews.body:
Thanks for the extra validation details. I still see a few code-level issues that look unresolved on the current branch:

`tools_rust/mcp_runtime/src/observability.rs:419-448`  
The new Rust observability bootstrap appears to assume OTLP is always the exporter. `build_tracer_provider()` always goes through `build_otlp_exporter()`, and `ObservabilityConfig::from_env()` only reads OTLP/Langfuse settings. That means a Rust-side deployment configured with `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=jaeger`, `zipkin`, or `console` would now fail at startup with an OTLP configuration error, even though those exporter modes are still supported on the Python side. I don’t see anything in the follow-up notes that addresses this compatibility regression.

`docker-compose.with-langfuse.yml:311-320`  
I also don’t understand how the Redis healthcheck is meant to work as written. The container is started with `--requirepass`, but the probe is still plain `redis-cli ping` with no authentication. If `redis-cli` enforces auth here the way I’d expect, `langfuse-cache` should stay unhealthy and the dependent Langfuse services would be gated on that. Since you mentioned the stack came up locally, there may be some image/CLI behavior I’m missing, but the compose file still looks inconsistent and I think the probe should authenticate explicitly.

`Makefile:1227-1238`  
The host-port preflight in `CHECK_PORT_SPECS` still doesn’t look idempotent for the Langfuse targets. It checks running services with `$(COMPOSE_CMD_MONITOR) ps`, but `make langfuse-up` / `make langfuse-monitoring-up` start the stack through `$(LANGFUSE_COMPOSE)`. So if the Langfuse stack is already running and already owns ports like `3100` / `3130`, a second invocation can still fail with a false “port already in use” error instead of recognizing those containers as part of the same project and reusing them.

`tools_rust/mcp_runtime/src/observability.rs:491-499`  
`normalize_http_otlp_endpoint()` also still looks brittle for explicit OTLP/HTTP endpoint overrides on `:4317` when a path is already present. For example, `http://collector:4317/v1/traces` is returned unchanged, so the HTTP exporter still points at the gRPC port, and other `:4317` URLs with custom paths can be rewritten into malformed paths after normalization. I didn’t see this addressed in the follow-up Rust/Langfuse notes either.

So I agree the OTLP/Langfuse hot path is in much better shape than it was earlier in the thread, but these four issues still look open from the current diff.

reviews.author: lucarlig
reviews.body:

Let’s open a follow-up issue for [the review comments](https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/pull/3900#pullrequestreview-4031409704) and explore whether:
- [`axum-otel-metrics`](https://docs.rs/axum-otel-metrics/latest/axum_otel_metrics/) (metrics)
- [`axum-tracing-opentelemetry`](https://crates.io/crates/axum-tracing-opentelemetry) (spans)

can help here.

commits.message:
feat: integrate Langfuse LLM observability via OTEL

Add Langfuse as an observability backend for ContextForge, receiving
traces via standard OTLP/HTTP. Follows the existing Phoenix overlay
pattern with a dedicated docker-compose overlay file.

New files:
- docker-compose.with-langfuse.yml: Complete overlay with 6 services
  (langfuse-web, langfuse-worker, langfuse-db, langfuse-clickhouse,
  langfuse-minio, langfuse-cache) using separate infrastructure to
  avoid coupling with ContextForge databases
- docs/docs/manage/observability/langfuse.md: Full integration guide

Modified files:
- Makefile: 7 new targets (langfuse-up/down/status/logs/clean,
  langfuse-monitoring-up/down)
- .env.example: Langfuse configuration section with all tunable vars
- docker-compose.yml: Document Langfuse overlay in profiles header
- docs/docs/manage/observability/.pages: Add to docs navigation
- docs/docs/manage/observability/observability.md: Add as recommended
  backend option

Key design decisions:
- OTLP/HTTP protocol (Langfuse does not support gRPC)
- Hyphenated service names (AWS S3 SDK rejects underscore hostnames)
- No host port bindings for infrastructure (only UI on port 3100)
- Auto-provisioned org/project/keys via LANGFUSE_INIT_* env vars
- Health check uses $(hostname) (Next.js binds to container hostname)

Tested with 13+ traces flowing from tool invocations and gateway
health checks into Langfuse v3.162.0.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>

fix: harden observability span API, Bearer redaction, and caplog tests

- Replace all direct span.set_attribute() calls with set_span_attribute()
  in a2a_service, gateway_service, mcp_client_chat_service, and
  resource_service to enforce sanitization and export policy
- Fix Bearer/Basic token redaction regex to handle quote delimiters
  in both Python (trace_redaction.py) and Rust (observability.rs)
- Fix caplog test fixtures to specify logger name explicitly,
  resolving interaction with module-level basicConfig
- Apply cargo fmt to Rust mcp_runtime
- Refresh secrets baseline

commits.message:
fix: skip Langfuse credential validation when observability is disabled

The Rust runtime's ObservabilityConfig::from_env() ran
validate_langfuse_configuration() unconditionally, before checking
the `enabled` flag. This caused the sidecar to fail at startup when
a Langfuse OTLP endpoint was present in env but observability was
disabled — the Python side already short-circuits correctly.

Guard the validation behind the enabled check to match Python parity.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
